title: Loomis Theorem
body_html:
Loomis Theorem

Let $A$ and $B$ be two real matrices indexed by $I\times J$, and assume that all entries of $B$ are positive. Then there exist $(x,y,v)\in \Delta(I)\times \Delta(J)\times \mathbb{R}$ such that $$ xA \ge v\,xB $$ and $$ Ay \le v\,By. $$

Here $xA$ and $xB$ are row vectors indexed by $J$, while $Ay$ and $By$ are column vectors indexed by $I$. Thus the first inequality says that player 1's mixed row $x$ guarantees the ratio level $v$ against every column, and the second inequality says that player 2's mixed column $y$ caps the same ratio level against every row.

MFoGT presents Loomis as an extension of von Neumann's minimax theorem. The canonical blueprint route in this library is the opposite: Loomis is proved directly by induction on $|I|+|J|$ (see the proof-plan Direct Induction Proof Of Loomis Theorem), and finite minimax is then obtained as the $B=\mathbf{1}$ specialisation (Minimax via the All-Ones Specialization of Loomis), because $xB$ and $By$ are both all-ones vectors for probability vectors $x$ and $y$. The alternative $t\mapsto\operatorname{val}(A-tB)$ route, which would derive Loomis from finite minimax, is therefore not used here.
proof_html:
The selected proof route is the direct induction proof. It constructs the extremal lower ratio $$ \lambda_0=\sup\{\lambda:\exists x\in\Delta(I),\ xA\ge \lambda xB\} $$ and the extremal upper ratio $$ \mu_0=\inf\{\mu:\exists y\in\Delta(J),\ Ay\le \mu By\}. $$ Compactness of the finite simplices gives attaining strategies, positivity of $B$ gives $\lambda_0\le\mu_0$, and the induction step rules out $\lambda_0<\mu_0$ by deleting a strict column or row and mixing the inductive strategy back into the original game. Thus $\lambda_0=\mu_0=v$, and the attaining strategies satisfy $xA\ge vxB$ and $Ay\le vBy$.

References

  • [MFoGT, Thm. 2.5.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Loomis theorem for matrices A and positive B.
